trust_decision.summary: Whether pdfioDictSetStringf stores a durable copy of its formatted stack buffer in the dictionary (via pdfioStringCreate) or the dangling stack pointer itself; decided in pdfio-dict.c pdfioDictSetStringf. AT THE PINNED COMMIT THE FIX IS ALREADY APPLIED.

landing_point.why: Advisory names dictionary string-formatting; pdfioDictSetStringf is the only formatted dict setter and it is the line the fix changes.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Other setters (pdfioDictSetString/SetName, pdfioArrayAppendString/AppendName, pdfioFileCreateStringObj) also store the caller's pointer without copying, but that is the library's by-design contract (callers pass durable strings from pdfioStringCreate), so a solver correctly leaves them alone; none is a route to the fixed flaw.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: pdfioDictSetString/pdfioDictSetName/pdfioArrayAppendString store caller pointers without copying (zero-copy contract); an over-broad fix that makes them copy or free changes ownership semantics for every caller.

O6_input_shapes: printf-style formatted string up to 8192 bytes (single shape)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: pdfioDictGetString converts a binary value through local temp[4096] and stores it back into the dict value; a copy that stored temp directly would be the same dangling-pointer mechanism.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same file, same pattern of local buffer then store into _pdfio_value_t; the real code correctly wraps it in pdfioStringCreate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A planted pdfioArrayAppendStringf/pdfioDictSetNamef formatting into a stack buffer and passing it to the zero-copy setter.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Mirrors the existing pdfioDictSetStringf/pdfioStringCreatef helpers; a maintainer adding a convenience variant could repeat the original mistake.

O9_family: memory safety: dangling pointer / use of stack memory after return (CWE-825)

O10_build.toolchain: autoconf configure + make, cc; zlib (libpng optional)
O10_build.project_tests: testpdfio.c (make test); no test of pdfioDictSetStringf found in the tree

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap the buffer in pdfioStringCreate(dict->pdf, buffer) (which is the correct, complete fix) or make the buffer static (not thread-safe, overwritten by later calls).
